outputs.explanation: This is a continuous stacked-area/bar representation of median state-frequency composition across many contiguous Pol II-level bins (n=5912 promoters partitioned into a large number of thin, gapless bins along a continuum). Functionally it behaves like a trend/line plot over an ordered continuous variable rather than a small-category bar chart of group means; overlaying thousands of individual promoter data points on a 100%-stacked composition across hundreds of bins would be unreadable and is not the type of chart this check targets (analogous to the line-plot exemption).

The single-molecule stack is a heatmap-like display in which every row is an individual DNA molecule (2952 molecules), so individual data points are already fully shown, not averaged over. The adjoining color sidebar just summarizes the composition of that same single-locus dataset (not an average across multiple loci/replicates), so the individual-points requirement does not apply.

Same representation as panel A (mouse data): a continuous, gapless stacked composition across many bins along an ordered continuum (Pol II ChIP-seq level), analogous to a line/trend plot and exempt from requiring overlaid individual points.

Same representation as panel B: each row of the single-molecule stack is an individual molecule (2871 molecules), so individual data are already displayed; the sidebar summarizes only this one locus's own molecules, not an average over multiple loci.
Boxplots inherently display the distribution (median, IQR, whiskers, and outlier points), and box plots are explicitly exempt from requiring separately overlaid individual data points.
